reason: The receiver seems suited to collecting carbon dioxide from the capture unit, addressing one of the two goals.
expectation: I expect the unit to fill or prepare the receiver with compressed carbon dioxide, though I don't know whether further steps will be needed.

alternatives.reason: Electrolysis also advances a goal, but I'm unsure why the water is used at a specific gas outlet.
The oxygen outlet might also start electrolysis, but its role is similarly unclear to me.

effect: The capture unit supplied compressed carbon dioxide and completed that goal; separating water remains.
reaction: Collecting an ingredient from the thin atmosphere is a satisfying detail.
reason: The hydrogen outlet is one of two available ways to advance water separation, though I don't understand why water is applied at an outlet.
expectation: I expect electrolysis to produce hydrogen, perhaps leaving oxygen to collect separately.

alternatives.reason: The oxygen outlet might also start the separation, but I have no clear reason to prefer it.

effect: The plant conditioned the water and collected hydrogen; the oxygen outlet collects the other stream from the same process.
reaction: That explanation clears up why water appeared at two outlets, though the interaction still feels a little odd.
reason: Collecting oxygen is the only offered combination and should finish separating the water.
expectation: I expect an oxygen supply and completion of the water-separation goal.

effect: Collecting oxygen completed the water-separation goal and clarified that the lander will use it as an oxidizer.
reaction: The distinction between oxidizer and fuel was a useful detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Collecting hydrogen was most worthwhile because the explanation clarified that both gas outlets belong to the same electrolysis process.

leastWorthwhile.text: Collecting oxygen felt somewhat repetitive after collecting hydrogen, although the oxidizer detail added something useful.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the oxygen collection was another interaction with drinking water at an outlet; the explanation clarified that it was the other stream from the same process.

arbitrary.text: Applying water at a gas outlet initially felt odd, although the later explanation gave the interaction a purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would want to see how the collected gases support the early return and what happens with the second ice core, though this chapter itself was quite brief.
